question.problem:
Let $△ABC$ be a triangle such that $m∠A=2m∠C$ and  $m∠B=m∠A+m∠C.$ 
Which of the following statements is true?
question.worked_solution:
Let $x$ be the measure of the angle $∠C,$ then $m∠A=2x$ and $m∠B=2x+x=3x.$

Since the sum of the interior angles is ${180}^{∘}$, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠A+m∠B+m∠C & ={180}^{∘} \\ 2x+3x+x & ={180}^{∘} \\ 6x & ={180}^{∘} \\ x & ={30}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠A & =2\cdot {30}^{∘}={60}^{∘}, \\ m∠B & =3\cdot {30}^{∘}={90}^{∘}, \\ m∠C & ={30}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, $△ABC$ is a right triangle because it has a right angle ($m∠B={90}^{∘}$).
